title: Love is a Dog from Hell (Poems 1974-1977)

vibeProfile.oneLine: Bukowski's plainspoken, profane poems of love, lust and loneliness.

summary: Bukowski's poems from the mid-1970s, plainspoken and profane, about love, lust, loneliness, drinking and the indignities of the body. Written in his stripped-down, conversational line, they find odd flashes of tenderness and truth in the gutter, refusing every poetic convention. Fans consider this one of his essential collections; newcomers will find the fastest way into why so many readers who claim to hate poetry make an exception for Bukowski.
whyReadIt: The fastest way in for anyone who thinks they hate poetry. Plainspoken, profane, and sometimes unexpectedly tender.

funFacts.text: Bukowski's conversational, no-frills style made him one of the best-selling poets in America.
